blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 73 in June to 51 in October (−30.1%), and it took 7.3% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 7 in June to 9 in October (+28.6%), and it took 0.5% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Cedar Hills for detached houses in October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Cedar Hills homes and market figures

Cedar Hills has no City-published neighbourhood boundary — the City of Surrey tags its Cedar Hills parks "Whalley and City Centre," and the name is anchored by Cedar Hills Elementary at 12370 98 Avenue and Cedar Hills Park at 12761 87A Avenue rather than by a plan map.

The commercial anchor is named in City documents: a 2026 City land-exchange document identifies the Cedar Hills Shopping Centre at 12830 96 Avenue, at the southeast corner of 96 Avenue and 128 Street, on a 14.6-acre site.
The east edge is 120 Street (Scott Road): a February 2025 City planning report for 12248 97 Avenue places the site about 400 metres from 120 Street and its R6 RapidBus stops.

Cedar Hills stock is detached houses on standard urban lots being split smaller: the February 24, 2025 planning report for 12248 97 Avenue (a 0.2-hectare site) proposed rezoning from Urban Residential (R3) to Small Lot Residential (R4) with a variance to reduce lot widths from 12 metres to 11.76 metres, creating four small lots with side-by-side garages and access from a future 96A Avenue.

The pattern is older than the current zone names: a 2013 City report for 12215–12229 96 Avenue proposed retaining an existing duplex and subdividing into six lots under RF-12 and a Comprehensive Development (CD) zone based on RM-D, with new access through a rear lane instead of 96 Avenue driveways.
The neighbourhood's green structure is older parkland: Moffat Memorial Park at 9434 122 Street was acquired in 1967 to provide park amenity and sports fields for the adjacent secondary school.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-lot subdivision here runs through rezoning plus variance, not as-of-right: at 12248 97 Avenue the R3-to-R4 rezoning, the lot-width variance and a 10-metre dedication for the future 96A Avenue were all conditions of creating four lots, per the City's February 2025 report.

Old Land Use Contracts still surface on Cedar Hills titles: LUC No. 118, adopted by Authorization Bylaw, 1975, No. 4472 on August 16, 1976, regulated the commercial lot at 128 Street and 96 Avenue, and provincial law terminated all Land Use Contracts on June 30, 2024, bringing the underlying C-8 Zone into effect.

The next plan layer is not yet written: the 9572 120 Street report notes the site sits within the future Scott Road Corridor Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP), whose timelines have not been determined — the east edge of Cedar Hills is planned under the Official Community Plan (OCP) alone until that NCP starts.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Moffat Memorial Park is a memorial, not just a sports field: the City records that volunteer John Thomas Moffat died in April 1969 when a concrete dugout being built by volunteers collapsed, and the park at 9434 122 Street — baseball diamond, multi-use field, parking from 94A Avenue — was named to commemorate him.

There are two "Cedar Hills" park names to keep straight: Cedar Hills Park itself is at 12761 87A Avenue, well south of the 96–100 Avenue core most buyers mean by Cedar Hills, and the City tags it Whalley and City Centre.

A future street is already on the plans: lots along the south side of the 12248 97 Avenue block face a planned 96A Avenue, and the 2025 application required a 10-metre dedication to build it — rear-yard plans on that block should assume the lane-street arrives.

The Scott Road edge has its own commercial application: 9572 120 Street, at the southeast corner of 96 Avenue and 120 Street on the Surrey–Delta border, is proposed as a 4-storey commercial building with ground-level commercial, offices and a childcare centre, rezoning from CG-1 to C-15 (application 7924-0229-00, report dated April 27, 2026).

blocks.text: Cedar Hills: development and new projects

items.t: 12248 97 Avenue — rezoning from R3 to R4 plus Development Variance Permit for four small residential lots with reduced lot widths (11.76 metres) and side-by-side garages, 0.2-hectare site; status: Planning Report dated February 24, 2025 recommending the rezoning bylaw proceed to public notification ahead of First, Second and Third Reading (as of November 3, 2026).

9572 120 Street (96 Avenue and Scott Road) — 4-storey commercial building with ground-level commercial, office uses and a childcare centre, rezoning CG-1 to C-15 with Development Permit and Development Variance Permit, application 7924-0229-00; status: planning report dated April 27, 2026 (May 11, 2026 council date), a resubmission of a previously defeated proposal (as of November 3, 2026).

Cedar Hills Shopping Centre land exchange — 12830 96 Avenue (14.6 acres) named as a proposed City disposition property in an Arena and Entertainment Hub land-exchange analysis; status: proposed transaction document dated June 26, 2026, with the City in discussions with the property owner — not an approved sale (as of November 3, 2026).

The R6 Scott Road RapidBus is the rapid link at the east edge: the City's 12248 97 Avenue report places the site about 400 metres from 120 Street stops served by route R6, route 319 (Scott Road / Newton Exchange) and route 312 (Scottsdale / Scott Road Station).

Route 316 (Surrey Central–Scottsdale) crosses the neighbourhood on 100 Avenue, 96 Avenue and 116 Street — the local route that connects Cedar Hills streets to Surrey Central Station without going to Scott Road first.
Driving, 96 Avenue is the east–west spine to Scott Road and Delta, 128 Street runs south to Newton, and King George Boulevard is reached west via 96 Avenue or south via 120 Street.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check for a terminated Land Use Contract on title before assuming the printed zone governs: on the 128 Street and 96 Avenue commercial lot, LUC No. 118 (1976) regulated use until provincial termination on June 30, 2024 brought the underlying C-8 Zone into effect — older Cedar Hills parcels can carry the same layered history.

Check the lot against Surrey's Development Permit Areas (DPAs) in the City's mapping (COSMOS): the Hazard Lands and Sensitive Ecosystems DPAs in Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 18020 can add geotechnical or streamside requirements a zone check alone will not show.

A streamside check is part of the same DPA screen: the Sensitive Ecosystems DPA covers streamside areas, so a Cedar Hills lot backing onto any creek or ditch should have its streamside setback area confirmed before a building envelope is assumed.

faq.q: Is Cedar Hills an official Surrey neighbourhood?
faq.a: Not with a published boundary. Buyers should fix a property by its street and zone, not by the neighbourhood label.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Cedar Hills house?
faq.a: Cedar Hills Elementary is the named local school, at 12370 98 Avenue, and the City's planning reports use it directly: a 2013 report projected two elementary students from a six-lot project to Cedar Hills Elementary, and the 2025 report for 12248 97 Avenue discusses Cedar Hills Elementary capacity. The paired secondary school beside Moffat Memorial Park is L.A. Matheson Secondary at 9484 122 Street. Catchments are still confirmed by address in the district locator.

faq.q: Can a Cedar Hills lot be split into small lots?
faq.a: Yes, but it took a rezoning and a variance in the worked example. At 12248 97 Avenue the owner proposed moving from R3 to the R4 small-lot zone, reducing lot widths to 11.76 metres, and dedicating 10 metres for a future 96A Avenue along the south property line. A buyer pricing a Cedar Hills lot on a four-way split is pricing an application, not an existing right.

faq.q: What is happening with the Cedar Hills Shopping Centre site?
faq.a: The City has named it in a proposed land swap. A June 2026 City document lists the Cedar Hills Shopping Centre property, 12830 96 Avenue, 14.6 acres at the southeast corner of 96 Avenue and 128 Street, as one of three proposed disposition properties in a land exchange connected to a proposed Arena and Entertainment Hub, with 10355 King George Boulevard as the proposed acquisition property. The document is a proposal analysis, not an approval.
